issue.title: Bug: [dualtor][vpp] Mux drop ACL ignores SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS — a single standby port blackholes the data plane on ALL ports

failure.body:
> **Note:** this issue originally reported the symptom as a possible drop-counter attribution problem, scoped to one test case. Investigation disproved that and found a far more severe root cause. The body below has been rewritten to lead with the confirmed finding; the full investigation trail is preserved in the comments.

Tracked under umbrella issue #26046. This is gap **(1)** of #28884, which was closed with only gap (2) fixed.

### Is it platform specific

vpp

### Importance or Severity

**High.** On a dual-ToR VPP deployment, a single mux port entering standby blackholes **all** data-plane traffic on **every** port of the switch. The box continues to look healthy — BGP stays up and mux HWSTATUS reads `consistent` — so the failure is silent.

### Description of the bug

`vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp` never reads `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS`. Because MuxOrch uses that attribute as the *only* mechanism scoping the mux drop ACL to standby ports, the rule degrades from "deny on the standby ports" to "deny on every bound port".

**How MuxOrch scopes the drop.** It creates a single shared table and a single shared rule for all mux ports, then edits `IN_PORTS` on each switchover (`orchagent/muxorch.cpp`):

```cpp
// port goes STANDBY -> add to IN_PORTS
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port, RULE_OPER_ADD);

// port goes ACTIVE -> remove from IN_PORTS
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port_, RULE_OPER_DELETE);

// last standby port leaves -> delete the rule outright
if ((port_set.size() == 1) && (port_set[0] == port_))
    gAclOrch->removeAclRule(table_name, rule_name);
```

Binding the *table* to all 32 ports is intentional and VPP honours it correctly. The bug is purely that the per-entry `IN_PORTS` qualifier is discarded:

| Layer | Intended scope | VPP behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Table -> port binding | all 32 ports (by design) | honoured |
| Entry `IN_PORTS` | standby ports only | **silently discarded** |

**The code path.** `acl_rule_field_update()` has no case for `IN_PORTS`, so it hits `default:`:

```cpp
sai_status_t status;
status = SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS;      // initialised to success

switch (attr_id) {
    /* SRC_IP, DST_IP, ICMP, L4 ports, IP_PROTOCOL, TCP_FLAGS,
       PACKET_ACTION, PRIORITY, ADMIN_STATE ... */
default:
    SWSS_LOG_ERROR("Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: %d", attr_id);
    break;                        // status still SUCCESS
}
return status;                    // returns SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS
```

It logs an error, then returns success — so orchagent believes the rule was programmed correctly and never retries or reports a fault.

`SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` = `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_START + 0xa` = `0x100a` = **4106**, and the DUT logs the miss at exactly the mux switchover time:

```
2026 Aug 18 <IPV6>.709047 vlab-vpp-03 ERR syncd#syncd: :- acl_rule_field_update: Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: 4106
```

(`show mux status` reports `LAST_SWITCHOVER_TIME 2026-Aug-18 <IPV6>`.)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Dual-ToR VPP KVM testbed, mux ports on `Vlan1000`.
2. Put a **single** mux port into standby: `config mux mode standby Ethernet8`.
3. Send data-plane traffic through any **other**, still-active mux port.
4. All traffic is dropped on ingress; RX_DRP climbs on the active port.

Inspect:

```bash
redis-cli -n 1 hget ASIC_STATE:SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ACL_ENTRY:<oid> SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS
docker exec syncd vppctl show acl-plugin acl
sudo grep -a "Unhandled ACL entry attribute" /var/log/syslog
```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual** — SONiC requests the deny on 1 port; VPP applies it to all 32:

```
ASIC_DB: SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS = "1:oid:0x1000000000034"   -> Ethernet8  (1 port)

VPP:     acl-index 3  ipv4 deny src <IP>/0 dst <IP>/0
         applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32                        (32 ports)
```

**Expected** — the deny applies only to `Ethernet8`; all other ports forward normally.

### Blast radius: the failure is binary, not proportional

Because MuxOrch removes the rule entirely once the last standby port leaves, the switch has only two states. Demonstrated live on `vlab-vpp-03`:

**One port standby (`Ethernet8`):**
```
acl-index 3  ipv4 deny src <IP>/0 dst <IP>/0
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32          <- entire data plane dead
```

**After `config mux mode active Ethernet8` (zero standby):**
```
acl-index 3  ipv4 permit src <IP>/0 dst <IP>/32     <- no-op placeholder, traffic flows
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32
```

So: **no port standby → everything works; any port standby → nothing works.** One switchover on one port takes out all 24 mux ports plus the 8 non-mux ports. This is why the dualtor_io results looked erratic — runs that kept every port active passed, and any run that put a single port into standby lost everything.

### Measured impact

From `tests/logs/08181110` (`test_normal_op_active_server_to_standby_server`), with only `Ethernet8` standby:

```json
{ "sent_packets": 5721, "received_packets": 0, "received_packet_diff": -5721 }
```
```
ERROR tests.common.dualtor.dual_tor_io: Sniffer failed to filter any traffic from DUT
```

Source server `<IP>` sits behind `Ethernet96`, which was **active**:

```
Address       MacAddress         Iface         Vlan
<IP>  <IPV6>  Ethernet96    1000
```

`portstat` — every other mux port sits at the RX_DRP 15 baseline; `Ethernet96` is the lone outlier at 5,736. Excess `5,736 - 15 = 5,721`, an exact match for `sent_packets`.

### Why the earlier #28884 fixes did not cover this

sonic-platform-vpp#272 (merged 2026-08-11) and sonic-sairedis#2029 (merged 2026-08-17) added an ip2me / receive-DPO bypass so **control-plane** packets escape the deny. That restored heartbeat/ARP/BGP, which is why mux ports reach `consistent` and the box looks healthy — and is precisely why this is easy to miss. **Data-plane** traffic has no such bypass. sonic-sairedis#2027 (`Permit local traffic ahead of ACL deny rules`) was closed unmerged.

Note the image under test (`master-29031.1192809`, built 2026-08-14) also predates the sonic-sairedis#2029 merge.

### Suggested fix

In `vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp`:

1. Handle `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` in `acl_rule_field_update()` — resolve the `objlist` of port OIDs to hwif names.
2. Bind the deny only to those interfaces rather than every interface the table is bound to, and rebind on each `IN_PORTS` update, since MuxOrch rewrites it on every switchover.
3. Make the `default:` case return a failure status for unhandled **match/field** attributes instead of `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS`, so a silently mis-programmed ACL surfaces as an error. Worth doing independently of the mux case — any future unhandled match field will degrade the same silent way.

### Output of `show version`

```
SONiC Software Version: SONiC.master-29031.1192809-6c879a32d
Build commit: 6c879a32d
Build date: Fri Aug 14 <IPV6> UTC 2026
Platform: x86_64-kvm_x86_64-r0
HwSKU: Force10-S6000
ASIC: vpp
```

Testbed `vms-kvm-dual-vpp-t0-1`, DUTs `vlab-vpp-03` / `vlab-vpp-04`, `active-standby` mode.

### Related

- #28884 — closed, but only gap (2) was fixed; this is gap (1)
- #29078 — same root cause, data-plane symptom
- #26046 — umbrella

resolution.title: [vpp][acl] match on ingress interface to support SAI ACL IN_PORTS
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Implements `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` for the VPP platform by fanning each ACL entry out into one VPP rule per named ingress port.

A VPP ACL rule has no notion of an ingress interface, so until now the field had nowhere to go: it fell through to the `default:` case of `acl_rule_field_update()`, which logs `Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID` and carries on. The entry was still programmed, just without the restriction, so it applied to every port its table was bound to.

That is the wrong direction to fail in. On a dual ToR the standby DENY entries name only the standby mux ports, so dropping the restriction turns them into a table wide deny and blackholes traffic on the active ports as well.

The matching VPP side is [sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp#278](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp/pull/278), which adds an `in_sw_if_index` field to the ACL rule. Design writeup: [sonic-net/SONiC#2506](https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/pull/2506).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/29077

`IN_PORTS` is how orchagent scopes an ACL entry to a subset of the ports its table is bound to. `aclorch` restricts it to physical interfaces, and the dual ToR standby DENY entries rely on it.

Silently widening those entries to the whole table is worse than not supporting the field at all, because nothing in the logs distinguishes a rule that was scoped from one that was not.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 39466368

#### How did you do it?

A VPP ACL rule matches one interface, so a SAI entry naming N ports becomes N VPP rules:

- `acl_entry_in_ports_get()` finds the attribute and resolves it. The cached attribute only carries the list count, its list pointer is still null, so the entry is read again with a buffer of the right size. Each port OID is then resolved to a VPP interface name via `vpp_get_hwif_name()`.
- `fill_acl_rules()` pops the rules it just generated for the entry and re-adds one copy per resolved interface. This is the same shape as the existing fan-out where a port based entry with no protocol becomes a UDP rule and a TCP rule.
- `vpp_acl_rule_t` gains `in_hwif_name`. The SAI layer keeps working in interface names, as it already does for binding, and `vpp_acl_add_replace()` resolves the name to a `sw_if_index` when it builds the API message. Empty means any.
- `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` becomes an explicit no-op in `acl_rule_field_update()`, since it is not a per rule field.

The fanned out rules stay contiguous from `ace.vpp_rule_base_index`, so `num_rules` still describes the entry and the counter aggregation in `getAclEntryStats()` sums over them unchanged.

Failure handling is deliberate, since three different things can leave the interface set empty and they do not mean the same thing:

| Case | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Field absent or not enabled | Not scoped, one rule as before |
| Enabled but names no port | Scoped to nothing, no rule emitted |
| Port list unreadable, or no port resolves | Error, ACL programming fails |

The last row matters. On failure the scope of the entry is simply unknown, and installing it unscoped would re-introduce exactly the blackhole this PR is fixing, so `fill_acl_rules()` fails and `CHECK_STATUS_ACLTBLCONFIG` leaves the previous ACL in place.

The empty list case is left as "matches nothing" on purpose: no ingress interface can be a member of an empty list, so emitting no rule is the faithful translation.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Built into `docker-syncd-vpp` and deployed to a `vms-kvm-dual-vpp-t0-1` dual ToR testbed, then checked the programmed rules against the mux state:

- `vlab-vpp-03`: 18 standby ports, 18 matching ingress scoped deny rules.
- `vlab-vpp-04`: 6 standby ports, 6 matching ingress scoped deny rules.
- ACL 3 stayed bound to all 32 interfaces in both cases, confirming the scoping comes from the rules and not from the binding.

Rule counts tracking the standby set on two ToRs with different mux distributions is the behaviour this PR is after, and is what regressed before.

Still outstanding: live downstream forwarding under mux toggles (standby → active → standby) has not been run yet, so the dataplane effect is verified by rule inspection rather than by packets.

#### Any platform specific information?

VPP only.

This depends on [sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp#278](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp/pull/278) and the two have to merge together. Adding the field changes the `acl_add_replace` message, and therefore its CRC, so a syncd built against one VPP version cannot program ACLs on the other. That PR also bumps `VPP_VERSION` to `2606-0.6`.

A scale note for reviewers: an entry naming N ports costs N rules, so a table bound to many mux ports grows proportionally. VPP's tuplemerge can additionally fold the fanned out copies into one less specific mask type, and `split_partition()` has no interface dimension to split them back apart on, so they can end up on a single collision chain. Correctness is unaffected, `single_rule_match_5tuple()` in the platform PR re-checks the interface on the collision path, but it is worth knowing before scaling the port count up.

### Documentation

Design is written up in [sonic-net/SONiC#2506](https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/pull/2506).
